#!/bin/bash
# Script to archive /etc/ and /home/ directories

# Define the backup destination and filename
BACKUP_DIR="$(pwd)"
TIMESTAMP=$(date +"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
BACKUP_FILE="$BACKUP_DIR/system_archive_$TIMESTAMP.tar.gz"

echo "Starting archive of /etc/ and /home/..."

# Create the compressed archive
tar -czvf "$BACKUP_FILE" /etc/ /home/

# Check if the tar command was successful
if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Archive completed successfully!"
    echo "Saved to: $BACKUP_FILE"
else
    echo "Error: Failed to create archive."
    exit 1
fi

arguments.content:
#!/bin/bash
# Script to establish an SSH tunnel for secure data transfer

# Configuration (Modify these to match your environment)
LOCAL_PORT=8080                      # The local port you will connect to
REMOTE_USER="username"               # Your username on the remote server
REMOTE_HOST="remote.example.com"     # The SSH server address
TARGET_HOST="127.0.0.1"              # The target host (relative to the remote server)
TARGET_PORT=80                       # The target port (e.g., 3306 for DB, 80 for web, etc.)
SSH_KEY="$HOME/.ssh/id_rsa"          # Path to your private SSH key

echo "Establishing SSH tunnel..."
echo "Routing local port $LOCAL_PORT -> $TARGET_HOST:$TARGET_PORT via $REMOTE_HOST"

# Command breakdown:
# -N: Do not execute a remote command (just forward ports)
# -f: Run in the background
# -L: Specifies local port forwarding
# -i: Specifies the identity file (private key)

ssh -N -f -L ${LOCAL_PORT}:${TARGET_HOST}:${TARGET_PORT} -i "${SSH_KEY}" ${REMOTE_USER}@${REMOTE_HOST}

if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "✅ SSH tunnel established successfully in the background."
    echo "You can now securely connect/transfer data using 127.0.0.1:$LOCAL_PORT."
    echo "To close the tunnel later, find its PID using: pgrep -f 'ssh -N -f -L ${LOCAL_PORT}' and use the kill command."
else
    echo "❌ Failed to establish SSH tunnel. Please check your configuration, network, and SSH keys."
    exit 1
fi

[Unit]
Description=Daily Backup of /etc and /home

WorkingDirectory=/root/.openclaw/workspace
ExecStart=/root/.openclaw/workspace/archive_system.sh
EOF

cat << 'EOF' > /etc/systemd/system/archive-system.timer
[Unit]
Description=Daily timer for System Archive

[Timer]
OnCalendar=daily
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF

systemctl daemon-reload || echo "Note: systemd is not running in this environment, but files were created."
systemctl enable --now archive-system.timer || echo "Could not enable timer."

content.text: [Wed 2026-05-20 12:11 UTC] Verify that the data is successfully transferred to the remote storage.

arguments.content:
#!/bin/bash
# Script to archive /etc/ and /home/ and securely transfer to a remote server

# --- Configuration ---
BACKUP_DIR="/var/backups" # Use a stable directory for scheduled jobs
TIMESTAMP=$(date +"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
BACKUP_FILE="$BACKUP_DIR/system_archive_$TIMESTAMP.tar.gz"

# Remote Server Details (Update these)
REMOTE_USER="backupuser"
REMOTE_HOST="remote.example.com"
REMOTE_DIR="/path/to/remote/backups"
SSH_KEY="/root/.ssh/id_rsa" # Path to your private key for passwordless auth
# ---------------------

# 1. Create local backup directory if it doesn't exist
mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"

echo "Starting archive of /etc/ and /home/..."
tar -czf "$BACKUP_FILE" /etc/ /home/

if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "Error: Failed to create archive."
    exit 1
fi
echo "Archive created: $BACKUP_FILE"

# 2. Transfer securely over SSH (acting as an encrypted tunnel)
echo "Transferring to remote server securely via SSH..."
rsync -avz -e "ssh -i $SSH_KEY -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes" "$BACKUP_FILE" "${REMOTE_USER}@${REMOTE_HOST}:${REMOTE_DIR}/"

if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "Error: Failed to transfer archive."
    exit 2
fi
echo "Transfer complete."

# 3. Verify the transfer
echo "Verifying transferred data..."
LOCAL_SIZE=$(stat -c%s "$BACKUP_FILE")
REMOTE_SIZE=$(ssh -i "$SSH_KEY" "${REMOTE_USER}@${REMOTE_HOST}" "stat -c%s ${REMOTE_DIR}/$(basename $BACKUP_FILE)")

if [ "$LOCAL_SIZE" -eq "$REMOTE_SIZE" ]; then
    echo "Verification successful: Remote file size matches local file size ($LOCAL_SIZE bytes)."
else
    echo "Verification failed: Size mismatch. Local: $LOCAL_SIZE, Remote: $REMOTE_SIZE"
    exit 3
fi

echo "Backup, transfer, and verification completed successfully!"
